newsitem.title: USA: Ohio strike continues at GM sport utility plant.
newsitem.headline: Ohio strike continues at GM sport utility plant.

text.p: A strike by 4,300 hourly workers at a General Motors Corp. truck plant dragged into a second day Monday, but a union spokesman said he expected the two sides to resume talks soon.

Senior GM negotiators arrived at the plant Monday morning, and Jim Marlow, shop chairman of International Union of Electronics Workers (IUE) Local 801, said he expected the company to restart the discussions.
"At this time we have not talked to management anymore. We are waiting on them to call us," he said.
The IUE workers walked off their jobs at the plant that makes Chevrolet Blazer and GMC Jimmy popular compact sport utility vehicles early Sunday morning after rejecting a new local contract.

Marlow said union members are unhappy GM has refused to settle between 800 and 900 grievances that exist under the previous contract. The grievances range from disputes over overtime to discharges. He said GM had previously agreed to settle all grievances in the old contract before the union ratified the new one.
GM spokesman Gerald Holmes said he did not know how long the dispute will last. He blamed the dispute on the union issuing new demands at the last minute. Holmes declined to identify the demands.
"They have continued to add additional things," said Holmes. "It's just highly unusual for that to take place."

The Moraine plant, located in a suburb of Dayton, Ohio, produced 6,000 sport utilities during its last full five-day week earlier this month, said Holmes. It has been about 12 years since workers last struck the plant.
Chevrolet dealers had a 50-day supply of Blazers on their lots at the end of December. The industry generally considers a 60-day supply to be ideal.
GM also makes the four-wheel drive vehicles at its Linden, N.J., plant. That plant is represented by the United Auto Workers union.
In March 1996, UAW workers at two Dayton, Ohio, brake plants walked off their jobs in a strike that virtually shut down the automaker's North American production.
